reason: The cited evidence describes DTA methodology for high-temperature ceramics (E2) and separate XRD techniques under pressure (E1) or on levitated samples (E3), but none demonstrates the proposed integrated DTA-XRD on HEAs, the claimed <±2% uncertainty, or the direct correlation between XRD and DTA signals during melting. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: DTA can measure melting temperature and latent heat with <±2% uncertainty for HEAs
In situ XRD can track crystallographic changes during melting of HEAs
XRD structural transitions will correlate directly with DTA latent heat signals
CALPHAD modeling can integrate DTA and XRD data to refine thermodynamic property extraction
High-throughput DTA-XRD is feasible for HEA compositional libraries
